feedback: The evidence supports the wheel_track change as the next test. Iteration 5 (entityR2B, 111.80) had slalom line loss of 0.10 and max_error of 0.0636 m, so line retention is under control at mass 0.8 and body_length 0.18, and the remaining failure is tracking at the limit. Iterations 1 to 5 all show max_error between 0.061 and 0.066 m, so the error is not moving with sensing or inertia, which points to turn authority. Iteration 4 (entityR2B, 124.20) showed that lowering inertia (mass 0.7, body_length 0.14) raised slalom line loss to 0.85, so inertia should not go lower on the slalom track without a line-loss check. I cannot state an outcome for the current candidate, which has not raced. Next steps depend on the next race. If max_error falls toward 0.06 m with line loss at or below 0.1, keep wheel_track 0.10 and consider a mass-only reduction to 0.7 with body_length 0.18, which cuts yaw inertia by about 12 percent (a smaller step than iteration 4's roughly 37 percent cut). If line loss rises to 0.2 or more on slalom, the higher turn authority is destabilising the line, so the next step is to hold the geometry and reduce kp rather than change the array. If max_error stays near 0.063 m with line loss near 0.1, the limit is gain balance, not geometry, and I will say so in the next request.
requested_changes: Keep wheel_track at 0.10 with the iteration-5 inertia (mass 0.8, body_length 0.18) and sensors unchanged, so this race isolates the track change.
If slalom line_loss_events is 0.2 or higher after this race, hold the geometry and let the Integrator reduce kp. Do not change sensors.
If max_error falls below about 0.062 m with line loss at or below 0.1, try mass 0.7 with body_length 0.18 as a smaller inertia step than iteration 4.
